clue.text: Senior officer and I hail RAF marches on manoeuvres

explanation.surface: A top commander salutes as the air force parades past on an exercise.

clue.text: A dispute right off in public sale

indicators.note: something that is off has been taken away, so the right is removed from the dispute

blocks.note: taken as written
a ruction is a noisy row or quarrel

explanation.surface: A row breaks out and fairness is lost at a public sale.
explanation.walkthrough: A ruction minus its R leaves UCTION, which follows A to give AUCTION.
explanation.definitionFit: An auction is a sale open to all comers where goods go to the highest bidder.

clue.text: Launch posh car with final part not seen in public

explanation.surface: A luxury car is unveiled to the public with its rear end hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: Rolls is everyday British shorthand for a Rolls-Royce, the byword for a posh car.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollout is the introduction of a new product or service to the market, its launch.

clue.text: Slam troubled land embracing distasteful and ultimately obsolete emblem

indicators.note: something troubled is disturbed, so the word land is stirred up into a new order
to embrace is to wrap your arms around, so the shuffled letters go round the next piece

blocks.note: to hammer is to criticise severely, to slam
taken as written, to be rearranged
sick humour is distasteful
the last letter of obsolete

explanation.surface: A critic attacks a troubled country for its distasteful, outdated symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled land is split in two, with the distasteful word sitting between its pieces; obsolete is a fair hint, since the Soviet symbol now belongs to history.
explanation.definitionFit: The crossed tools were the symbol of Soviet communism, so the phrase names a famous political badge.

clue.text: Grounds for believing study going into European depravity

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
vice is wickedness or depravity

explanation.definitionFit: Evidence is the facts or information that support a belief or show it to be true.

clue.text: Lord’s house that’s said to show style

blocks.note: a manor is a lord's country estate and its house

explanation.surface: A nobleman's mansion is said to display good taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Manner is a way of doing something, a person's mode or fashion of behaving.

clue.text: Precinct with one tree adapted for emergency facility?

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: such a centre is one kind of emergency facility.
explanation.definitionFit: A reception centre houses refugees or evacuees arriving after a disaster, a place for crisis care.

clue.text: Shock coverage?

blocks.note: surface reading: news reporting of a startling event
setter's reading: a shock is a thick mass of hair, and this item covers it

explanation.walkthrough: Shock as a mane of hair, not a surprise, and coverage as something worn over it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine mesh worn over the head keeps a mass of hair in place, literally covering it.

clue.text: Lavish bill to be settled — about time

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: An extravagant invoice must be paid sometime soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settled' reads as paying the bill; it is the signal to rearrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal can mean generous or plentiful, as in a liberal helping, so it matches lavish.

clue.text: South American doctor’s put by pass needed by old Scotsman

explanation.definitionFit: A Colombian comes from Colombia, a country in the north-west of South America.

clue.text: Get up with cold leg?

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals that leg is defining a limb by example.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb is to go up, ascend, so it matches get up in the sense of mounting.

clue.text: Combined chant after time passes

indicators.note: when something passes it goes away, so the time letter leaves the chant

blocks.note: to intone is to chant in a monotone
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A group chant rings out after time runs on.
explanation.walkthrough: INTONE without its T gives IN ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something all in one unites several parts or functions together, so the phrase means combined.

clue.text: This writer pronounced batsman to be startling phenomenon

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken, so the writer's word is heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: this writer is the setter, who would say I
an opener is a batsman who starts a cricket innings

explanation.surface: A columnist declares a cricketer a stunning sensation.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the opening batsmen face the first balls of an innings.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-opener is a revelation, something surprising that changes how you see things.

clue.text: Greek character gets straw matting for bird

blocks.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
thatch is a roof covering of woven straw or reeds

explanation.surface: A Greek gets straw matting to line a bird's nest.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuthatch is a small woodland songbird that climbs tree trunks head first.

clue.text: Firearm recoiled many times, used by investigator

blocks.note: PI stands for private investigator
lots of times means many times

explanation.surface: A detective's gun kicked back repeatedly in use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recoiled' wants to describe the gun firing, but it is the signal to read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistol is a small handgun, a kind of firearm held in one hand.

clue.text: Flat, perhaps — small verbal joke that’s unsophisticated

blocks.note: a flat is one example of a home
S is the abbreviation for small
a pun is a play on words

explanation.surface: A dull, small wordplay gag lacks any polish.
explanation.walkthrough: Flat looks like an adjective meaning dull; it is the noun for an apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Homespun originally meant cloth woven at home, hence plain, simple and lacking refinement.

clue.text: Stay with two bridge players in trip

blocks.note: a ride is a short journey or trip

explanation.surface: Two card players travel together and settle in for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: RIDE holds ES as R(ES)IDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside is to live or dwell somewhere, to stay there as a home.

clue.text: Mechanical corrosion overwhelms old boy in charge

explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon carries out operations in a hospital operating theatre, so a performer there.

clue.text: Fantastic tenor and another briefly entering company, source of music

taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.walkthrough: 'Another briefly' means a second tenor cut to its abbreviation, T, as on a choral score.

clue.text: Bill with a cost largely obscured for sauce

taken as written
cost without its final letter

clue.text: Seasoned food served up in Lima — lashings!

blocks.note: the letters spanning the two words

explanation.walkthrough: Lashings is British slang for plenty, as in lashings of ginger beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a cured sausage flavoured with garlic and spices, a seasoned cold meat.

clue.text: Place in military unit journalist holding award

explanation.definitionFit: To embed a reporter is to attach them to a fighting unit so they cover a war from inside it.

clue.text: An early form of fuel?
